question: Does a depicted socket contain actual space for the retained prongs, independently of the attachment relation?

retained_visual_replicas.prior_attachment_score: Both passed the depicted plug-on-front-socket criterion
retained_visual_replicas.source_observation: The strip housing remains a solid box/loft. Socket marks and plates are positive surface geometry. No corresponding receiving cavities are removed from the body.

text_only_controls.source_observation: Both responses construct blind cavities directly in a closed manifold mesh rather than using surface marks or Boolean modifiers.

verification: Exact Boolean intersection of evaluated meshes, calibrated on a solid block (84 volume units of collision per prong), a shallow recess (60) and a clear receptacle (0). Both audit executions pass all three calibration types. Original scene hashes remain unchanged.

inspection_views.method: Named occluding parts are hidden only for the derived view; the retained source scene and its geometry are not changed or saved over. Metadata records every hidden object.

interpretation: Relational fidelity and volumetric receptacle geometry are independent assessment axes: a visually seated plug can still collide with solid plastic.

These two text-only controls demonstrate available cavity-construction capability under an explicit functional specification. They do not demonstrate spontaneous preservation of that property from an image.

The visual reconstruction protocol allowed overlapping solids and excluded mechanical fit. The collision audit adds a separate functional criterion without changing the previous attachment scores or claiming prior instruction noncompliance.

The evidence supports investigating why image-based reconstruction selected surface symbolism while direct functional requirements produced negative-volume geometry. It does not uniquely identify an internal model mechanism or establish the cause of the original author's unavailable mesh.
A clear final pose is necessary but insufficient for a general insertion-path, manufacturing or electrical claim.
